utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you see the order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that that order was dated on the 6th of December, 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. Prosecutor. Can you repeat that? I didn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that that order was dated the 7th of December, 1992 -- 6th of December, sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I would like to draw your attention to paragraph 4 of this order. It deals with artillery support.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that the Bregava Brigade could request artillery support from the 3rd HVO Brigade and the 1st Knez Domagoj Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's pass on to another topic a little bit. Witness, is it fair to say that after the international conference on Vance-Owen Plan, which did not solve territorial or military aspect and didn't become a valid international instrument, the HVO unleashed a widespread anti-Muslim campaign?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, [redacted], not the chief of staff or the commander of a military district. I didn't occupy any high position. I can give you my personal positions, but personally, I would not agree with that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit 213.1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have it, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I would like to direct your attention to item 4 of the order.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And I've got two questions stemming from this item. First of all, which orders of HVO headquarters and south-east operative zone did you mean in that order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I cannot remember, so I can't answer your question. But here, what I meant was that I expected some danger, so I elevated the degree of combat readiness. And the numbers of the orders that I had received are given under item 1, and the expected danger - I apologise - I'm trying to thwart the expected danger by this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it was your order, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe that this was my order. I would be able to tell you something more if I saw the original, but I believe that this could be my signature, so I do believe that this is my order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree that this order was issued after the correspondent order issued by Bruno Stojic after Vance-Owen talks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not confirm this, Mr. Prosecutor. This order involves operative, military things. It doesn't involve any politics. So without any -- with reference to some tragic events in the Central Bosnia, similar things were moving towards my unit. I was warned by the headquarters, by the Main Staff, who warned me about these incidents, and this order was issued to prevent any possible incidents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And my second question --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And if such incidents should occur, then the order has to be followed in the way it is written.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean that some persons, units, should be disarmed and isolated? Right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, those who jeopardise my unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whom did you mean? Muslims? The Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't mean Muslims. Who I had in mind were the armed members of the Bosnia and Herzegovina Army. That is where I expected problems to come from.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And I would like to -- the witness to be shown Exhibit 216.6.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you see this order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like you to pay attention to items 4 and 5, particularly in item 5 --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You ordered that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Particularly in item 5, you ordered that all army moves must be reported urgently; is it correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it also correct that Bregava unit moved its headquarters to their previous position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What do you mean by the "previous position," Mr. Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I mean its headquarters as determined in the order dated the 6th of December, 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot confirm this, Mr. Prosecutor. If they acted upon orders issued by the operative zone southeast Herzegovina, they would not imply or mean any danger. Or if they respected the order that they were given, then they would have meant a problem for me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct, Witness, that somewhere in the middle of April, you started issuing orders aimed at removing Muslim forces, Muslim soldiers, from your area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, could you please be more correct in expressing yourself? What do you mean by "removing"?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Okay. I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit 297.1. 297.1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see this request?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that request signed by you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like you to explain this order. Just take into consideration my previous question when we didn't understand each other.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the beginning of my testimony, Your Honours -- I am not clear on item 1. What does that item imply? I am not sure that this item was in the original document. Mr. Prosecutor, Your Honours, item 2, to prevent entrance and passage of motorised vehicles into the zone of responsibility of the 1st Brigade, to confiscate and issue the necessary documentation, what is disputable in that? An army which presents a danger to another army cannot, without the consent of the former army, enter its area. In the army, this is called a silent occupation, an occupation without fighting, which was attempted. So this order was issued with that intent. Item 4, to immediately disarm members of BH, so not Muslims, not civilians, but armed members of the army, to be disarmed, not killed, and weapons to be stored in a warehouse, because that was my -- these were my weapons. The Republika Srpska army tried to do the same thing, to occupy the area from Muslims and from Croats, and now the same method was being applied by the BH Army, according to our estimates.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Now I would like witness to be shown Exhibit 301.4 and 301.5.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They are identical in nature, and what I'm interested in, just to hear an explanation from you, why did you order to arrest soldiers in BiH uniform and detain them for 15 days? Was it a sort of preventive isolation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I believe that I remember something similar. Thank you. The document is now in front of me. Two documents are now in front of me, both dated the 16th of April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's correct, but one is called a sort of request with demand, and the second one is an order.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I expect your response to my question about preventive isolation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry that I interrupted the witness. It never says in this order "preventive isolation," and this is what the witness is expected to say in his answer. So I just wanted to warn my learned friend that he is speculating in his question, i.e., that his question is speculation and that he cannot expect an answer to this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Rephrase your question, Mr. Prosecutor. I think you asked that question before, or you would like to hear the explanation from the witness why did he order to arrest soldiers in BH uniform and detain them for 15 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes. I expect a response from him. And why I am uttering these words, "preventive isolation," this is our Prosecution case, that people were arrested without any reason, justifiable reason. So I'm putting forward my case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. But lead this witness step by step.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, Witness, was it absolutely necessary to arrest soldiers in BH uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this your response?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can, and I wish to clarify, but my answer to your question is: We did not arrest them because they wore BH Army uniforms. But, Your Honours, Mr. Prosecutor, you have in front of you two documents. One is a request, the other is an order. The request is addressed to the military police. And the order, because it is a unit that I didn't command it, I requested from them, and I issued the order to my unit. In the left corner, bottom, you can see who the documents were sent to, and also at the bottom you can see that it was also sent to the Bregava Brigade. So in the order I say that no entry should be allowed to the armed BH Army members into our area of responsibility without my written clearance. This is under item 1, Mr. Prosecutor. All members of the BH Army should be arrested and all their weapons and equipment should be confiscated. What does that mean, Mr. Prosecutor? This means that this implies only to the movements of armed units which want to enter my area of responsibility unbeknown to me, without my consent. You can also come by the documents in which I, at the same time, allowed the same unit to pass through my area of responsibility by issuing similar orders. So what is disputable? If I don't know that an army unit wants to enter my area of responsibility, I can imply that they are endangering my area of responsibility. If I know about their movements, then their movement is not disputable.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But do you agree with me that your order provided for arrest and detention of BH soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of armed men, Mr. Prosecutor, and those who were attempting to carry out things that were not allowed, forbidden acts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what do you mean by "a newly arising situation"? I mean in the part, let's say, prologued your order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, this newly arisen situation is a new situation. That means that any new moment would bring and ask for new solutions. What we expected were problems. From various sources we received information in relation to the plans of our neighbours. We saw the very same type of problems in Central Bosnia, and we undertook preventive measures. That means we wouldn't do anything or attack anyone or imprison anyone, Mr. Prosecutor, that is, those who come with clear and clean intentions. But those with ill intentions, they would be imprisoned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, is it correct that in that period of time, the situation in Stolac area and in your area of responsibility on the whole was relatively calm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Relatively, yes, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit 302.1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a report from your commander, Mr. Lasic, on the situation in his zone of responsibility, including Mostar, Stolac, Capljina. Do you agree with this evaluation of the situation by Mr. Lasic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, the situation was changing from day to day. How could I now remember one single day among so many others in some year, what happened exactly and what the situation was?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But is it correct that on the same day, you also issued an order which provided for mopping up BH forces with all available resources?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot recall that, Mr. Prosecutor, unless I am shown a document, unless I see a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I just want to make sure that we are talking about P302.1. Are we speaking about this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: No. We are passing on to another document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think we are between this document and the next document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes. You are right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is because what Mr. Prosecutor just said is not written in this document. I cannot find it. I don't know which document you mean, that what you said is not written anywhere, absolutely anywhere. I don't know where you got that from. Where did you get that statement from? That's why I'm asking you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, this trial has been going on for 14 months. I think as earlier, as the normal practice, the Prosecutor will put his case to the witness first, and demanding an answer from this witness, and after that, the Prosecutor might show a document to the witness concerning this question. I believe Mr. Prosecutor will come to that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: You're right, Your Honour. Thank you very much. I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit 302.2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you see this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I would like you to explain to me, what did you mean, while issuing that order, by "mopping up"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, in the previous order that we did not comment, at the very end of the order by Mr. Lasic, whether I agreed with his opinion in item 4, there was talk of a lot of problems and shooting in Mostar, about the borders, and this went all the way up to the centre of town. This is one thing. Second thing is that the conflict, and the clashes from central Bosnia were coming nearer to the south, were approaching. And the third thing, the order that you're speaking about came about, and I believe that this is correct, it came about in specific circumstances, and it is a result of a specific situation. I said, Your Honours, to start with, yesterday, about a more general situation, when I mentioned that the Bregava Brigade attempted to enter the area of Dubravska Visoravan, of Dubrava, in a peaceful way, and we found out that this would be attempted in several locations, and I said what we attempted and what we did in this way. They were not going to be thwarted in their intent, and this is one of the orders in a series of orders which was written as in a form of a warning, of a threat, that we would attack them if they continued, if they persisted in doing what they were doing, unless they were respecting the orders that, at the time, they had agreed with. And under item 1, you can see that their command post was not positioned in accordance with an agreement and that it was a threat for me, that they were still trying to go towards the south, and that what that meant is that they continued doing that, for the tenth time that I would answer, that I would respond with all means available. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you resort to military actions in respect of Bregava Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is, I cannot recall the date exactly, but yes, we did something similar, bearing in mind that, again, after this order, I did not use force immediately. I tried to frighten them again, to warn them, to move them away from that area with peaceful means, and after that gave no results, and I used two companies, unless I am mistaken. I arrested a member of this brigade who was in a position where he was not supposed to be in, and who had plans about attacking us. And these are the documents that I'm talking about, and this was Pizovic that had plans about attacking us, that is that we attack them only a couple of days before they had carried out a planned attack on us. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to you take an at Exhibit 431.2. This is --

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I would like the Deputy Registrar to provide the witness with this document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Prosecutor. If I may ask, whose document is this? What is this about? And what is the date of the document?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. This is an ECMM report, and I would like to direct your attention to items 7, 8. We have it in both English and B/C/S translation. The B/C/S translation just in front of the original document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But I don't have the Croatian version. At least I don't. In the binder, I do not have the Croatian or the B/C/S version of the document 431.2. I am talking about the ECMM report.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Maybe you have it on the front page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: No. I checked very carefully.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, in my bundle I only have the second page of the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: The B/C/S version is on one page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But it started from item 7, 8, not --

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, 7, 8, both are translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Where is the first page? I mean, the English translation, we have the title, we have the 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 items there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, but we have only translated the relevant parts of the document, not the whole document, not the whole ECMM report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Prosecutor, you could use this document, but later on, you have to furnish the first page to the Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Even that our witness speaks English? I thought that we would not have any problems with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, he's entitled to have that document in his own language, but you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you have this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor. I have it in both Croatian and in English, but I cannot establish the date when this document was written.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 3rd of June, 1993. You will find it in the original English version of the document, in the upper left corner.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I've got two questions to you. Is the situation with Bregava Brigade you just described to us, is consistent with your story, described here in the document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I would like to comment on the whole of the document and then include this question as well. I think that this document was not written with good intentions or that it is correct for a large part. First of all, my command was never located in the village of Dabrica. The village of Dabrica is located on the Serb side. That is, it is on Bosnian Serb Army positions. And the second insinuation which reminds me of some contestable questions with the gentleman from the army, when we were negotiating by the end of the war, and throughout the war, continuous insinuations that we had links to the Army of Republika Srpska and that we were hoping to attack the army together, the BH Army, together. Now, the second insinuation in relation to the location of my command post, it is true that we were faced with both armies, and it is also true that the current line was stable. Now, the question of opening the passage at that time, I believe, Mr. Prosecutor, that is not at all correct. What was correct is that the Serbs had called on us through a small portable radio. They called my soldiers, not me, on the first line, and they offered help. They said that they would use artillery against BH Army if we asked for that. Your Honours, believe me, this had never occurred to us. This is an insinuation. And this is one of the documents which was also delivered to the BH Army, and this is one of the documents -- that was a reason, one of the reasons for increasing the tensions and the conflict. So this means that the penultimate item -- it is true that it is in this way that we resolved the problem with the Bregava Brigade in this way. The member who was not arrested, he again reformed the unit and he again attacked us and caused us a lot of casualties by the rest of the war, and he used civilians and army members particularly on the Dubrava plateau.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And my next question, just pertaining to this document, is: Is your position, as quoted here in the document: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [redacted] is it reflected correctly in this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Prosecutor, we have to warn you that we are in the open session and that this witness is under the protective measures.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Awfully sorry. It should be removed from the transcript, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know that my learned colleague did not do this on purpose, but this has occurred so many times on the side of the Prosecutor. I believe, my rough estimate, this has happened about five or six times. This is a serious submission, and I would like to ask Their Honours how they would react if this had happened to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think the Prosecutor made an apology already, and he has already said that he will be very careful in the future proceedings that he will not disclose the identity of the witness. We'll have that redacted. You may proceed, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, Witness, I'm waiting for your response to my second question about your position as a partisan of military methods of solving problems, as reflected in this document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor and Your Honours, I do not agree with this statement, with this -- what is written in this item. Any military commander has been taught that if he assesses and if he sees that he has available information, which is reliable, that he would be attacked, that his forces would be attacked, that he is the one who should attack first. Why is that? Now, am I to wait for the opponent to kill all my men and then to react? And then, Your Honours, you would then charge my opponent and try my opponent because he has killed my men. That means that any normal soldier would react first. And, Mr. Prosecutor, if this was not true, I can tell you that I'm one of the first people to join the joint army in Sarajevo before peace was declared, so that Bosniaks and Croats would make together an army so that we would have an Army of Federation. So we wanted to be on this together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness. Let's pass on to another topic. Witness, is it your testimony that Muslim soldiers were with you, I mean with your brigade, until the 13th of July, 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, a number of them remained after that date as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will it be fair, Witness, to say that you started expulsion of Muslim soldiers from your unit long before the 13th of July, 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor, as a result of the assessment that they represented threat, danger, after the events involving Bregava Brigade and all that happened in Central Bosnia and all the bloody conflict in Mostar, Central Bosnia. So according to the assessment, we thought that that could happen in the same way, and in the brigade that we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I would like witness to be shown Exhibit 493.01

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, have you read this order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not yet, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You may take your time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So was it your order that a minimum number of Muslims should stay in every unit? Right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor, but the order goes on. But it says those who were from the start with us, who had shown and proved to be good, and who, according to the -- who are known by their commanders and for whom they can be guaranteed that they wouldn't turn against us. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct, Witness, that on the following day -- not -- sorry. Some days later, you issued another order providing for expulsion of all the Muslims from your unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is possible, Mr. Prosecutor, but if I see the order, then I would be able to tell you more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I would like the court deputy to show the witness Exhibit 498.2.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So on the 6th of July, you already issued an order to remove all Muslims from the unit, right, irrespective of their background and participation in joint battles against the Serbs; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The authenticity of this order, Mr. Prosecutor, is in question. There are some strange things on here. On this document I can see four seals, and I'm not quite sure what this is about. You can see at the end a sentence which really isn't clear to me either, that people who had participated in the action are to be disarmed and sent home. Is this in relation to the Muslims who had been with us and who had participated in actions? Are they to be disarmed and sent home? And this is in contradiction with item 1 of the order. So I cannot do this so quickly and really assess what this is all about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But do you see a signature at the bottom of the page?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it your signature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Possible, Mr. Prosecutor. But, as I've said, there are two items here which go one against the other, which are mutually exclusive: item 1 and the remark on page 2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you say is mutually exclusive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To remove and disarm all members of the army who are Muslims. That's under item 1. And under 2, that people - that's in the remark - people who participated in the action to be disarmed and sent home. Only that. Does that maybe refer to those Muslims who, together with us, participated in all the previous actions? I believe that this may refer to this category of soldiers. However, Mr. Prosecutor, I would like to say one more thing. When we received information that the BH Army, i.e., the Party of Democratic Action commands over the BH Army and that they were preparing themselves to launch an attack on us, in the previous order you could read one item, and that was that Muslims should be kept but should not be assigned any important duties in the command, in the security. And at the end it proved to be correct and it proved to be wise, because we came by documents, at the moment when we captured some members of the brigade, showing that they had been preparing an attack on us. And that's, Mr. Prosecutor, when we found among those documents the lists of soldiers showing the names of those members of my unit who were receiving my salary. So at the same time they were on two lists: on the list of the Bregava Brigade and on the list of the brigade that I don't want to mention, but the brigade that I am talking about all the time. So they were on the lists of both brigades. On the 13th of July, when they finally attacked us, all of this that I'm talking about got its confirmation, was confirmed. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, is it correct that by this order, I mean issued on the 6th of July, you abolished the first item of your previous order issued on the 3rd of July, and there is no contradiction between these two orders now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Mr. Prosecutor. That was never implemented to the end because in all units, until the end, there was a relatively high number of Muslim soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, is it correct that further along, you also issued an order relevant to Muslim conscripts to be arrested and detained?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is possible, Mr. Prosecutor. I don't know which order and which conscripts and which period you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit 509.3.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see this order? Was such kind of order issued by your unit command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, you can see that this order was not signed by me. It is possible that at that time I was absent. However, such an order may have existed. I believe that it was not -- never followed through, but I can explain all the elements contained in this order. Mr. Prosecutor, with regard to the previous document, I said that, at the moment, there was a large number of Muslim Bosniaks, Bosniak members of our brigade. All that time, if some individuals and some groups were following the platform of the SDA, they joined the ranks of the BH Army, and as they did that, they also committed different crimes in order to justify their membership in the HVO once they joined the BH Army. They did that in order to be able to tell their new fellows-at-arms how many Croats they had killed. To my judgement, I believe that we kept all those Muslims for whom we believe that they would not turn their arms against us. Before this document was issued, a sabotage group turned their barrels against their former colleagues and friends. They massacred them. They opened fire on dead bodies of those they had killed. They mutilated them. You have minutes compiled by SFOR who carried out an on-site inspection, in the period. After that, they infiltrated deep into our ranks, committed murders. I can't give you the names of all the places and people so tragically killed all over the area. And as a result of all those activities, we had to put up ambushes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, but I would ask you to be concise in your responses because of the constraints of time. My next question is: Is it correct, Witness, that your anti-Muslim actions were not limited to former soldiers of HVO of Muslim nationality, military-aged persons, but the whole Muslim population in the adjacent area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know what activities you are implying. If you are referring to arrests, the army did not participate in that, and whether some military investigative organs thought that an individual had to be arrested, whether somebody else detained people, I really can't confirm. I can't tell you that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit number 559.2.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that this person whose signature is under the order was a commander of the 3rd Battalion, part of your brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I can only confirm that the person with this name exists and that this person was the commander of one of the battalions. As to whether this is his signature and -- I find it incredible, as well as the rest of the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why do you find it incredible?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, a document like this cannot be without a seal, and that is the first thing that strikes me as unusual. The next thing that is unusual is the fact that no normal person would write item number 2 and sign it, to say, "When rounding them up, do not pay attention to their age." That is something that nobody normal could even think, let alone write or carry out. And the third thing, Mr. Prosecutor, under item 3, two detention centres are mentioned, although there were never any detention centres anywhere. The person who was in the area - and this person was in the area - to make a mistake when writing the name of a place is something that is unacceptable from a soldier, from a commander. Further on, if this commander, if any commander, issues a verbal order, it doesn't make sense that his first subordinate issues a written order. For somebody like that to issue a written order, he had to address his superior. If a subordinate acts upon the order of his superior, he has the right to ask for a written confirmation of a verbal order. Sometimes a verbal order can be issued but only exceptionally, when there is not enough time to issue a written order. So all of the items in -- contained in this order are really not credible.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit 559.7.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is an order issued on the 5th of August by this same commander, again with reference to a verbal order, of the identical contents but which provides for a wider area of responsibility, and wider area of actions, where Muslims were supposed to be rounded up and arrested.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I think the same of this document as of the previous one. The army never participated in the arrests of any civilians. I agree that it may have occurred that during the capturing of some groups of soldiers, some civilians may have been arrested, and later on we tried to put that right urgently. And believe me, I see this for the first time, and I can't tell you anything about this. I cannot confirm this order, and I cannot believe in the credibility of this document, in the authenticity of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, could I interrupt here while we are on the point?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: My understanding is that the witness said to you that he rejected the authenticity of the first of the two documents that you're referring to, for a number of reasons, one of them being -- as I understood the transcript to say, one of them being that there were no detention centres at that time. Could you follow that up with more cross-examination, please? Because that doesn't appear to correspond with the documents that I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, if you allow me, I will do that but at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: At a later stage, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I thank you for -- I thank Judge Clark for asking the right question at the right time. I didn't want to intervene and I don't have the transcript in front of me. We heard in our headphones, according to the first order, 559.2, the witness said clear and loud that the collection centres that are mentioned in this order did not exist. So that these two mentioned in this order, the collection centres mentioned in this order, did not exist. And that is one of the reasons why he found this order incredible and surprising, because he knows very well that these two particular collection centres mentioned in this particular order never existed. That was what he disputed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We will come to that issue at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, one more question to the witness in respect of Exhibit 559.7. Again, this item 3, maybe it will shed some light on the issue. Gather detained person in collection centres to be determined by the commanders of the 2nd and 3rd Companies.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, item 3 means that the commanders who have approximately 70 to 80 men under them, should determine where collection centres will be. I am really not clear on this. There was never such a possibility. It was not a realistic possibility. There is no military logic to item 3, none whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But anyway, you see this item in the order?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have to react. The witness said that he has never seen these two documents, that he contests their authenticity, but the questions continue on these documents, although the witness told us very clear why he did not find these two documents credible. Why does the Prosecutor insist on continuing examining the witness on these two documents? After very correct cross-examination, now I can say that I must say that the witness cannot be asked questions about something that he doesn't know anything about, that he has never seen, and disputes the credibility of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe that the witness is going to tell us something about this document. Witness, you may continue to answer your question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have nothing further to say about any of these two orders. The Defence counsel really repeated what I said at the beginning, and that is that these two orders are not authentic. I cannot confirm their authenticity. There are so many things in them that go against the military logic, that I really don't know what to say but that I have never seen them, I don't know anything about them, and I really believe this not to be possible, these two orders not to be real and possible orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, is it correct that in July and further, you had some contacts with the representatives of international organisations, including ECMM, and you had some conversations with them relevant to the issue, I mean to the Muslims being arrested, detained, pushed from their area? Right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, it is possible that we had such talks, but the issues discussed, we can talk about.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I would like witness to be shown Exhibit 493.3. There is a B/C/S translation in front of the first page of the document. I'm interested in item number 6. The document dated on the 4th of July.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you read it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that by the 4th of July, 1993, all the Muslims from your unit - units, I would say - had been removed, as you said to the representatives of the international organisations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that you claimed that all males from the age of 18 to 60 had been arrested?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I cannot confirm the authenticity of this document, and I cannot recall the gentleman who allegedly compiled this document. But it does say clearly in the document that the army did not participate in this but that it was somebody else, not subordinated to me. And this statement, although allegedly issued by me - and I don't recall ever having said that - it is still something that I heard from somebody else. So it is a secondhand statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, what we want to hear is what the witness is going to tell us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly, Your Honours, but can I please find out who the author of this report is? We don't know the source of this document, who is its author. So I would humbly ask you to assist me with that, and please can we have some insight from the Prosecutor as to the author of this document. We cannot have in this courtroom any document just for the fact that it comes from the Prosecutor. And again, I don't have the translation of the entire document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe that document explained the source for itself, and it's very clear on that. We'll turn to this question at a later stage, when the Prosecutor is going to tender this document into evidence. You may proceed, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to complete one topic before the break, and then I will not take too long after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I hope.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you agree with me that as a result of anti-Muslim measures undertaken by the HVO and you, your brigade, as part and parcel of the HVO, the Muslim population of Stolac area had significantly reduced by August/September 1993 came?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't agree with that, Mr. Prosecutor. This is a distortion. When you attack somebody and when you get, if you will excuse me, your butt kicked, then it is your own fault; it is not the fault of the one that you have attacked. But this was not carried out by the brigade, Mr. Prosecutor. A number of Muslims, Bosniaks, at the beginning of the war, fled the area. A number of them fled the area during combat activities and a number of them fled even during the peacetime. The fact is, Mr. Prosecutor, that the army attacked us, and we have documents to prove that. We were attacked and we suffered huge losses. If there were any ugly things among the Croatians, I am ashamed of them, but I didn't participate in them. I am the commander of a certain unit of the army. I was not the commander of the area. I was not responsible for the civilian police. I was not responsible for the crimes committed by other people. There were other institutions which I believe had a bearing on the things that you implied in your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, but you should agree with me that it was your orders, your orders, just to arrest and detain Muslims, no matter who executed those orders. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I agree with just one part of that, Mr. Prosecutor: to arrest those who pose a safety threat. Your Honours, Mr. Prosecutor, they were all armed. I agree that not all of them posed a security threat. However, Your Honours, an army does not have the right, does not have the means to carry out investigations. It is somebody else who has the right and the means to do that. Those organs who had the right to do that were not under my authority. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit 534.2, page 6. Page 6, item 3. It's only in English, but it's a very brief, short passage. The document dated 24th of July, 1993.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the page and the item that you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: With pleasure. Page 6, item 3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you read it in English? You may need the assistance of an interpreter.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't need the assistance of an interpreter. I understand it in English. Mr. Prosecutor, a little while ago I said, clearly, that the army did capture those for whom they thought that they presented a safety threat. At the same time, one part of the brigade was on the line facing the army of Republika Srpska, which really was a respectable opponent. I also said that I was not the commander of the area and I did not have any authority over the civilian, military police, or anything. Similarly, it never occurred to me to participate in the destruction of religious objects, let alone did I do it. I am ashamed that the religious objects were destroyed, and all of them were destroyed, Muslims, Croats, and Serbs alike. If that is positive, in Capljina, where I live, in my neighbourhood, the church still stands and is in good repair. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, but will you agree with me that this passage from the document deals with the ethnic cleansing in the area carried out by the [redacted]?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But, Mr. Prosecutor, if you read this well, you will see that this again is the classical distortion of a thesis. It says here that the HVO lost over 30 men while cleansing the area from Muslims. And I repeat, for I don't know which time, that we did lose some 30 men, but that was during the attack carried out by our former friends, our neighbours, our former colleagues, together with those who had arrived and joined them. They carried out attacks on the HVO in several dozens of places, and that is when these soldiers lost their lives. After that, there was no major killing of Croats. I'm talking about the attack of Bosniaks on the HVO on the 13th of July. After that, several dozens were killed, but in the groups of one to three, and at different time intervals, ranging from one to three to seven days. So this, Mr. Prosecutor, is not a correct statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit 670. This is the last question before the break. And, Your Honour, I think that we should go into private session, because this document was provided to us under Rule 70 restrictions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I humbly ask how long the cross-examination will last? This is already lasting two and a half times longer than my direct examination. I think perhaps we should keep to what Mr. Scott said, quoting the Rules, and I was glad that he did, and it says that, according to the Rules in this Tribunal, that the cross-examination should last as long as the direct examination. But now this cross-examination is lasting two and a half times longer. I believe that we have a right to know how long the Prosecutor intends to continue his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Prosecutor has promised us that he will finish his cross-examination as soon as possible after the break. And would you please be kind enough to inform us how long you are going to last in your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: If you give me 45 minutes, I will be happy, to cope with my task in this period of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, during the break, try to reorganise all those documents and try to finish it as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So we'll break now. We'll resume at a quarter to 12.00, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, is it correct that in the beginning of July, you issued an order to release all Serb prisoners from the detention facilities in Stolac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did hear my question, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I did hear your question but I really cannot recall that I had ordered such a thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I would like witness to be shown Exhibit 493.2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, have you read the exhibit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see your signature at the bottom of the document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it's your order. Can I conclude that this order was issued just to free space for Muslim prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I did declare solemnly that I would tell the truth, even if it is detrimental for me, but I really cannot tell you what this is all about. If I could see the original, perhaps I would be able to tell you a little more, but as far as I can recall very quickly, I really cannot remember whether there were any Serb prisoners, and if there were any Serb prisoners, in my opinion at that time, this may have been just a couple of people so I really don't know what this is about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it also correct that in May, 1993, Kostana Bone Hospital in Stolac was also liberated from patients who were staying there for a long period of time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know anything about this subject, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. If you don't know, you don't know. I will not pursue this question any longer. Is it correct that in the beginning of July, you took the Dretelj prison and barracks under the control of your brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. Prosecutor, could you repeat your question? There was an interruption in the link.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, is it correct that on the 2nd of July, 1993, you issued an order according to which you took control of Dretelj prison and Dretelj barracks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't think this is correct, Mr. Prosecutor, but if I see the order, then I'll explain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is Exhibit 492.1.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it also correct that one of the addressees of this order was commander of the active police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does it mean that your orders were mandatory to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The question, Mr. President, is not at all in relation to what our relationship was, the relationship between the commander of the brigade and the active military police. What I mean is -- if Your Honours will allow me, I can explain this order. This is about when a unit or an institution comes to a new area, if some basic questions have not been resolved, it is normally relying on the institution which is the closest. That is me. That is my brigade. I was the closest. If I remember well, I got an order from my superiors to take out 40 of my Home Guards and that I would second them to the commander of the military police, and this order was addressed to my people, and it was for the information of the commander of the military police. That means that I was ordering my people, 40 of my men, to be resubordinated to the commander of the military police in Dretelj, that is, that they would work in accordance with their orders, that they would be answering to him - I'm sorry - and that if they had anything else -- if they needed anything else, logistically speaking, that is, quartermasters, logistics, anything like that, additional weapons, then my deputies for logistics, that is, the commander of the Home Guards, that they would then resolve this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, is it correct that you issued an order prohibiting to release any prisoners without your written permission?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor, I remember this very well, and if you'll allow me, I will explain. I heard, I learnt, from my associates and from some Muslims, some Bosniaks who I knew very well, who came to me and who told me what was going on there. So they told me then that some lower-ranking commanders, commanding officers, even some soldiers, what they did was that they were releasing prisoners for money, which means that they were making money out of those people who some of them I had captured, I had arrested. So I reacted emotively. This upset me a great deal, and I tried in this way to put some order, put this right. The meaning of this order is that some commanding officer cannot just decide like that about who will be released, or rather, who is guilty and who is not guilty. This is the job of the military investigating organs. What I gave myself the right to was to get involved and to try and put this injustice right. But, Mr. Prosecutor, very soon after that I received direct orders from my superiors that I had no business interfering, that I had no connection whatsoever, and that they would perhaps take into account my suggestions in relation to the matter whether some of those people I had captured were guilty or not guilty. Now, if we look at the lists, they said that if they compared the lists, that if they saw that there was a mistake, there was an error, that then they perhaps would put this right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, is it also correct that at some point, as the commander of Sector South, you also tried to assume responsibility for releasing prisoners from other prisons? I mean not only Gabela, Dretelj, but also Ljubuski and Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's correct, Mr. Prosecutor, but I believe that you can see from this that this was an emotive, an emotional reaction on my part, and how clear it is that I had no authority or no competence over this. I tried to take responsibility for this, to set things right, and also to speed up the investigation procedures, but, as I said, I received the order that this was not my job. This was not something that I was to do. In these camps, I got the impression that the investigation procedures were not speedy enough, that certain things were not being checked, and I had really ordered something for which I didn't have the right, which was never implemented, and the response I received was adequate.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit 493.02.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is the order we were talking about, right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I mean the order --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, okay. You may explain.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a different order with the -- an identical objective, Mr. Prosecutor. I received information that certain things were happening in these camps, apart from prisoners being released, that there were other ugly things that were happening, like taking the money, that is the robbing of those detainees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... sorry, I don't think that we should discuss some of these issues. I agree with your previous statement that that was a reason why you issued such kind of order. At least that's the explanation you give to us. Is it correct that you issued this order as a commander of Sector South in July, 1993? Blank pages inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French English transcripts. Pages 14820 to 14827.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think this is correct, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And also I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit 498.1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you seen this order? There is a reference to your name in item 5.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it also correct that you did not allow to visit Dretelj to representatives of media and international humanitarian organisations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's not right, Mr. Prosecutor. This order was written in order to prevent all kind of irregularities, setting things right, and all other things I would allow personally. So I did not want to allow visits without my knowledge, so that there would be no incidents whereby somebody could be taken away and that he -- this person could then be killed or that he would then be sold off for money or some other stupid goings-on. And again, telling you, Mr. Prosecutor, these few orders, I issued when I was very upset, when I was very emotional, but I underscore this, immediately I received from my superiors the order that this was not my job and that I had no right to issue such orders. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, when you are talking about your superior, whom do you mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I really cannot recall from whom I received such orders that the camps were not within my area of competence and that the military police was not within my authority, that this was the job of the military investigation bodies and that I should move away from this. Thank you. Whether this was Ministry of Defence, or what would be normal, Mr. Lasic, or perhaps the police, I'm afraid at this time I really cannot tell you who signed this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I would like witness to be shown Exhibit 498.3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you see this order, this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that this order came from Mr. Coric, Minister of Interior? Yes, military police, sorry, chief of military police.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I really cannot confirm this. I cannot confirm the authenticity of the signature of Mr. Coric, Mr. Prosecutor. If I recall correctly, I received at least a couple of similar orders, that is announcements, pieces of information, but whether this was such an announcement, I cannot tell you from memory. But this was the form that I received some orders in, that this was not within my area of competence and that this was not my job, thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to direct your attention to item 3 of this order. Is it correct --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that all the prisoners who were in military remand prisons, and who were captured by your units, could be released only with your written consent? Sorry, with your consent?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's not correct, Mr. Prosecutor. It says here very clearly that perhaps they would be released, perhaps be released with my consent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's what I'm asking you. Witness, did you ever visit Dretelj and Gabela detention facilities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I remember, Mr. Prosecutor, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know that conditions of life for prisoners were appalling there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Mr. Prosecutor, not appalling. I do not agree with this claim. First of all, they were not within my area of competence. Secondly, in some elements, they were relying on me, and when the administration, that is the military police, asked for doctors to be sent or to help in terms of medical help, I would do that. I would send a doctor. So they were relying on me, in terms of medical support. And they were also relying for some part, at some point, in terms of food. Now, Mr. Prosecutor, the food that was going to the camp of Gabela was the very same food that my soldiers were eating. Now, as to -- as for Dretelj, I know that - I heard it, I did not see it; I did not see either one or the other - in Dretelj, there was a kitchen, and I know that people who were cooking this food and prepared, they were making as much food as was needed, and it was my logistics that was sending the food and the necessary things. Now, there were problems with food and water in both places. I remember that there was an intervention. I remember that there was an intervention in relation to some problems in Gabela, but I really cannot recall at this moment what that was specifically, and I do remember that I intervened for it to be resolved. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, is it correct that on one occasion Gabela prison was visited by some representatives of HV, Croatian Army, on Mr. Bobetko's order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours and Mr. Prosecutor, I remember this very vaguely. I remember Mr. Dzanko, that he was asking questions about this, but I really cannot remember, ten years later, exactly what happened, because there were hundreds of things that happened during one day. But I'm asking you to help me remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit 565.6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if you'll allow me, I would like to say that this is a new document, and perhaps I could comment on this, that we don't have any idea about this. There's no signature. There is not any kind of sign to tell us who had written this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I would object, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can object, Mr. Prosecutor, but this is a basic thing. We have to know what this is. Otherwise you can put in any kind of paper and then we can work from that, even a paper that I would write. There's no signature. There's no seal. We have no idea where this comes from. What's this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, do we have to every time remind you what the Rules are? Have you forgotten in three or four weeks? Not in front of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, I believe that all the documents used in the proceedings are new documents. There's no doubt about that. From the B/C/S version, on the right-up corner, we saw a seal which indicates the Zagreb archive. So we have no doubt about this document. You may proceed, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, have you read the document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Is this the visit by Mr. Dzanko you meant in your testimony today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And according to this document, you visited Gabela together with Mr. Dzanko; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. I'm sorry, I really do not remember, but I am sure that what it says in here I did not see with my own two eyes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you see that it is reported in this document that you personally entered the camp, saw the facilities --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: It doesn't say that, Mr. Prosecutor. It says specifically --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: But he stayed outside, at his own request.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you told by Mr. Dzanko about what he had seen inside?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I said five minutes ago, very clearly, that if my memory serves me well, Mr. Dzanko asked for an intervention in Gabela, for some help, and that I said before I even saw this document. I don't know what the specific problem was at the time, but he did intervene, and I had to act upon his intervention. I remember that I did administer some sort of help. I did have to put something right, but I don't remember exactly what that was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, is it correct that apart from prisoners of war, male, Muslim males, there were females in Gabela?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I never heard of that, believe me. At the beginning of the conflict, I told my assistants to check whether there were any sick people, whether there were any females, whether there were any young people or elderly people, and if there were, that they should be released immediately. I couldn't order that, but I could exert my influence for this to be done. I remember I ordered that to my assistant for security, but that was at the very beginning, but not at this time in question. At this time I had already received my orders to stay clear from that, because that was not my job. I never heard any such thing. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit 607.11.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, have you read it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see the information that all the detainees slept on a concrete floor and that there were older persons, women, and children?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that, Your Honours, but I repeat that this is just one in a series of very unusual unsigned documents. But I would like to comment upon it. I have already said that I heard about some bad things happening there. Of some I did hear, of some I didn't. I tried to resolve those things that I had heard of. It says in here that they received two blankets, Mr. Prosecutor, if that is correct. To my mind, this proves that nothing was planned in advance. If it had been planned, we would have had beds there. But I sincerely doubt the truthfulness of such information, and I doubt the competencies of the people who wrote this. When you try to organise an army, you have to equip the army, and it takes 10 to 15 years, and the same goes for security services. If you recruit primitive, illiterate people into your security services, then you cannot expect them to issue competent reports, and it is only that kind of people that were recruited into the security services at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, did you have any other powers in respect of prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember, Mr. Prosecutor. Can you please help me to remember? I don't know what you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct, Witness, that prisoners from Gabela and Dretelj detention facilities were involved in some job on the confrontation line and they needed permission from you to allow prisoners to be taken to such kind of job?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, you have asked me several questions. I'll try to take them one at a time. It is correct that they were taken to work. Some commanders, a few of them, asked for my consent to take some prisoners who would help them carry out some work, because they didn't have enough people. It happened on several occasions. The next thing I would like to clarify is the fact that none of these people were harmed. We ever found ourselves in a farcical situation. None of the groups who worked on the line, not on the front line but in that area, were never put into -- under any danger. They were never humiliated. One of these groups even managed to escape. That's the extent of the humiliation they had to suffer and that's the extent of control that was exerted over them while they worked.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit 524.3 and 564.3.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I ask one thing? Can I ask for a clarification? We have been listening during this cross-examination and I would like to know what is the relevance of this cross-examination with regard to the indictment against my client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: My response will be quite plain, credibility of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Prosecutor, if you are aiming in this direction, my suggestion is that you could cut your -- cut short your cross-examination because, you know, we almost reached the time you promised.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, but I would like just the witness to give a response.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Try to finish your cross-examination as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I will try to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, Witness, do you see that, for example, from Exhibit 524.3, that detainees were involved, engaged for fortification and clearing of the forest?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you take a look at another document, again, cutting wood in the wooded zones before the front area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree that such kind of jobs is not [inaudible] Geneva Convention?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Incorrect, Mr. Prosecutor. Mr. Prosecutor, I agree that the first order may not be clear enough but the document, the second document that we are talking about, is perfectly clear. I don't know what this is. It looks as if some of my reports --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, the witness is answering the question. I think the witness will help us to clarify these things. Do you have something to add?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm just saying that we have frequent interruptions. The witness starts answering, then one or two words are lost, and then we get the third word. So we don't get the complete translation. I would like to ask the witness to repeat everything from the beginning, because some words have been lost, and I think it is in the interest of all of us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if you will allow me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I think that's a reasonable request. Witness, you may answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. The first order that we are talking about may not be clear enough in one of its parts, but the second document that we are talking about is -- although it's not very clear to me, I'll try to explain. If this is an authentic document, it clearly says that the detainees will be engaged only for the cutting of the wood, and that -- and full stop. So this is not dangerous and this is not humiliating. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But witness, take a look at item 5 of this same document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I can see that, Your Honours. Item 5, in the military terminology, does not have to mean that the detainees will be taken to the front line. The front line does not have to be the first line. The front line consists of several lines. The fact is, Your Honours, that none of the detainees were harmed, in no way. None of them were either injured or wounded. One group even managed to escape. That's how well they were guarded.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Now I would like witness to be shown Exhibit 565.03.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see that on this occasion, prisoners were sent to work on the defence line?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, on the defence line, but in the military terminology, it is a very elastic term. Look at the last sentence in which it says that the commander of the 3rd Battalion is going to take these men over and provide security for them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you agree with me that it is not allowed by the Geneva Convention to use prisoners of war on any war-related jobs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
